proposals: Each of the fourteen states’ industries departments should publish a quarterly statement of SGST-linked subsidy claimed, sanctioned, paid and pending, by scheme and unit size, so arrears like Telangana’s ₹4,250 crore are visible in official documents rather than surfacing through news interviews.

GSTN should provide a standard, downloadable certificate of net SGST paid in cash, after input tax credit, for each GSTIN and claim period, so every state computes the subsidy base the same way and disputes like Jharkhand’s 2019 restriction over buyers’ ITC have a common reference.

Each state should write into its industrial policy that later amendments do not reduce incentives for units already approved under earlier terms, so investors like the Hajipur unit in Bihar do not have to go to the High Court to collect a reimbursement the state had already promised.

The Himachal Pradesh Industries Department should publish the draft of its replacement investment policy, including SGST terms, for consultation before the current extension ends on 12 October 2026, so investors are not left planning against a lapsed 2019 policy on serial short extensions.

Haryana’s Industries and Commerce Department should notify the SGST sub-scheme under its 2026 industrial policy with a stated effective date, so the 30–70% share and durations now known only from secondary sources can be read in a notified text.
